'''Streebog''' ({{langx|ru|Стрибог}}) is a [[cryptographic hash function]] defined in the Russian national standard [[GOST]] R 34.11-2012 ''Information Technology – Cryptographic Information Security – Hash Function''. It was created to replace an obsolete [[GOST (hash function)|GOST]] hash function defined in the old standard GOST R 34.11-94, and as an asymmetric reply to [[SHA-3]] [[NIST hash function competition|competition]] by the US [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]].<ref name="streebog">[https://www.streebog.net/ GOST R 34.11-2012: Streebog Hash Function]</ref> The function is also described in RFC 6986 and one out of hash functions in [[International Organization for Standardization|ISO/IEC]] 10118-3:2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iso.org/standard/67116.html|title=ISO/IEC 10118-3:2018 IT Security techniques — Hash-functions — Part 3: Dedicated hash-functions}}</ref>

==Description==
Streebog operates on 512-bit blocks of the input, using the [[Merkle–Damgård construction]] to handle inputs of arbitrary size.<ref>[https://mjos.fi/doc/saarinen_stribob.pdf StriBob: Authenticated Encryption from GOST R 34.11-2012 LPS Permutation]</ref>

The high-level structure of the new hash function resembles the one from GOST R 34.11-94, however, the compression function was changed significantly.<ref>[http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.380.318 Algebraic Aspects of the Russian Hash Standard GOST R 34.11-2012]</ref> The compression function operates in [[Miyaguchi–Preneel]] mode and employs a 12-round [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]]-like cipher with a 512-bit block and 512-bit key.  (It uses an 8×8 matrix of bytes rather than AES's 4×4 matrix.)

Streebog-256 uses a different initial state than Streebog-512, and truncates the output hash, but is otherwise identical.

The function was named '''Streebog''' after [[Stribog]], the god of rash wind in ancient Slavic mythology,<ref name="streebog" /> and is often referred by this name, even though it is not explicitly mentioned in the text of the standard.<ref>[http://protect.gost.ru/document.aspx?control=7&baseC=6&page=1&month=6&year=-1&search=&id=180209 Full text of GOST R 34.11-2012 standard] {{in lang|ru}}</ref>

==Examples of Streebog hashes==
Hash values of empty string.
 <span style="color: green;">Streebog-256("")</span>
 0x 3f539a213e97c802cc229d474c6aa32a825a360b2a933a949fd925208d9ce1bb
 <span style="color: green;">Streebog-512("")</span>
 0x 8e945da209aa869f0455928529bcae4679e9873ab707b55315f56ceb98bef0a7 \
    362f715528356ee83cda5f2aac4c6ad2ba3a715c1bcd81cb8e9f90bf4c1c1a8a

Even a small change in the message will (with overwhelming probability) result in a mostly different hash, due to the [[avalanche effect]]. For example, adding a period to the end of the sentence:
 <span style="color: green;">Streebog-256("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]]")</span>
 0x 3e7dea7f2384b6c5a3d0e24aaa29c05e89ddd762145030ec22c71a6db8b2c1f4
 <span style="color: green;">Streebog-256("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]].")</span>
 0x 36816a824dcbe7d6171aa58500741f2ea2757ae2e1784ab72c5c3c6c198d71da
 <span style="color: green;">Streebog-512("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]]")</span>
 0x d2b793a0bb6cb5904828b5b6dcfb443bb8f33efc06ad09368878ae4cdc8245b9 \
    7e60802469bed1e7c21a64ff0b179a6a1e0bb74d92965450a0adab69162c00fe
 <span style="color: green;">Streebog-512("[[The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog]].")</span>
 0x fe0c42f267d921f940faa72bd9fcf84f9f1bd7e9d055e9816e4c2ace1ec83be8 \
    2d2957cd59b86e123d8f5adee80b3ca08a017599a9fc1a14d940cf87c77df070

==Cryptanalysis==
In 2013 the Russian Technical Committee for Standardization "Cryptography and Security Mechanisms" (TC 26) with the participation of Academy of Cryptography of the Russian Federation declared an open competition for [[cryptanalysis]] of the Streebog hash function,<ref>[http://www.streebog.info/ Open Research Papers Competition dedicated to analysis of cryptographic properties of the hash-function GOST R 34.11-2012]</ref> which attracted international attention to the function.

Ma, ''et al'', describe a [[preimage attack]] that takes 2<sup>496</sup> time and 2<sup>64</sup> memory or 2<sup>504</sup> time and 2<sup>11</sup> memory to find a single preimage of GOST-512 reduced to 6 rounds.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/375.pdf |title=Improved Cryptanalysis on Reduced-Round GOST and Whirlpool Hash Function (Full Version) |author=Bingke Ma |author2=Bao Li |author3=Ronglin Hao |author4=Xiaoqian Li }}</ref> They also describe a [[collision attack]] with 2<sup>181</sup> [[time complexity]] and 2<sup>64</sup> memory requirement in the same paper.

Guo, ''et al'', describe a [[second preimage attack]] on full Streebog-512 with total time complexity equivalent to 2<sup>266</sup> compression function evaluations, if the message has more than 2<sup>259</sup> blocks.<ref name=counter-revisited>{{cite conference |author=Jian Guo |author2=Jérémy Jean |author3=Gaëtan Leurent |author4=Thomas Peyrin |author5=Lei Wang |date=2014-08-29 |title=The Usage of Counter Revisited: Second-Preimage Attack on New Russian Standardized Hash Function |conference=SAC 2014 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/675 }}</ref>

AlTawy and Youssef published an attack to a modified version of Streebog with different round constants.<ref>{{cite web |title=Watch your Constants: Malicious Streebog |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/879.pdf |author=Riham AlTawy |author2=Amr M. Youssef }}</ref> While this attack may not have a direct impact on the security of the original Streebog hash function, it raised a question about the origin of the used parameters in the function. The designers published a paper explaining that these are pseudorandom constants generated with Streebog-like hash function, provided with 12 different natural language input messages.<ref>[https://tc26.ru/upload/medialibrary/efb/streebog_constants_eng%20Rudskoi.pdf Note on Streebog constants origin]</ref>

AlTawy, ''et al'', found 5-round free-start collision and a 7.75 free-start near collision for the internal cipher with complexities 2<sup>8</sup> and 2<sup>40</sup>, respectively, as well as attacks on the compression function with 7.75 round semi free-start collision with time complexity 2<sup>184</sup> and memory complexity 2<sup>8</sup>, 8.75 and 9.75 round semi free-start near collisions with time complexities 2<sup>120</sup> and 2<sup>196</sup>, respectively.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/539.pdf |title=Rebound attacks on Stribog |author=Riham AlTawy |author2=Aleksandar Kircanski |author3=Amr M. Youssef }}</ref>

Wang, ''et al'', describe a collision attack on the compression function reduced to 9.5 rounds with 2<sup>176</sup> time complexity and 2<sup>128</sup> memory complexity.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Zongyue Wang |author2=Hongbo Yu |author3=Xiaoyun Wang |date=2013-09-10 |title=Cryptanalysis of GOST R hash function |journal=Information Processing Letters |volume=114 |issue=12 |pages=655–662 |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/584 |doi=10.1016/j.ipl.2014.07.007|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2015 Biryukov, Perrin and Udovenko reverse engineered the unpublished S-box generation structure (which was earlier claimed to be generated randomly) and concluded that the underlying components are cryptographically weak.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Biryukov|first1=Alex|last2=Perrin|first2=Léo|last3=Udovenko|first3=Aleksei|date=2016|title=Reverse-Engineering the S-box of Streebog, Kuznyechik and STRIBOBr1 (Full Version)|journal=Cryptology ePrint Archive |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/071}}</ref>
